sentences.text: (DICTATED IN THE OPEN COURT)

Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Shri Jayant Prakash Patel, learned counsel for the appellant instead of pressing I.A. No.25321/2025, which is the first application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant Anil Baniya S/o Shri Devi Ram Baniya,
prays that this appeal be heard finally.

2. Accordingly, I.A. No.25321/2025 is dismissed as not pressed and with the consent of the parties,
this appeal is heard finally.

3. This criminal appeal under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is filed by the appellant Anil Baniya being aggrieved of the judgment dated 09.12.2023 passed by learned Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Scheduled Caste/Scheduled NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16195 2 CRA-5263-2024 Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989) Betul, District Betul in case No.SCATR No. 191 of 2020, whereby learned trial Court has convicted and sentenced the present appellant as under:

Shri Jayant Prakash Patel, learned counsel for the appellant submits that a consensual relationship between two adults has been treated to be an offence under the POCSO Act and conviction and sentence has been recorded, which is contrary to the evidence that has come on record.
It is submitted that, both the parents of the victim PW-2 & PW-4 have admitted that the victim was an adult at the time of the incident.
The victim (PW-1) has herself admitted that, she had gone with the appellant on her own volition at 11:00 p.m., without informing anybody at her house and had performed marriage with the appellant.

When these facts are taken into consideration,
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16195 3 CRA-5263-2024 then positivity of DNA vide Ex.P-24 in a consensual relationship is not sufficient to record and maintain the conviction.
Therefore, prayer is made to record a finding of acquittal.

5. Ms. Shweta Yadav, learned Deputy Advocate General for the respondent/State, in her turn,
submits that DNA Report (Ex.P-24) is positive, therefore no indulgence is called for in the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, as far as, consent of the victim is concerned, victim (PW-1) in para-3 of her cross-examination admitted that, when she was working with her parents, who were indulging in preparation of bricks, she had become friends with Anil.
They were talking to each other over phone also.
Thereafter, she admitted that after her returned to her original village, she continued to talk with Anil over the phone.
Anil had not visited her house but had met her outside the village.
She admitted that, she had taken Anil to the house of one Sandeep Marskole.
Anil had come to her village at 11:00 p.m. when she had gone out of her house while her parents and relatives were sleeping.
She admitted that, she had gone to Pilikalar along with Anil on his motorcycle and had not raised any alarm.
She also admitted that, when she had performed marriage with Anil at a temple, then she had not informed anybody at the temple about any misdeed being done by Anil.
She admitted that she has an elder sister and elder brother at her house.
Her elder brother is about 02-03 years elder to her and her sister is about 04-05 years elder to her.

The father of the victim (PW-2) in para-5 of his cross-examination admitted that, his marriage was performed 24-25 years ago.
After one year of his marriage, his eldest child was born.
The victim is his third child and the age gap between all the three children is 01 year each.
He further stated that, he had recorded date of birth of the victim on estimation.

8. The mother of the victim (PW-4) has corroborated the evidence of father (PW-2) and admitted that her marriage was performed 24-25 years ago and she has three children with age gap of one year each.
9. Shri Narmada Prasad Sahu (PW-5), Headmaster of the school admitted that, victim had taken admission in the sixth class and had recorded her date of birth on the basis of transfer certificate.
He stated that he does not know, as to on what basis, date of birth of victim was recorded in the earlier school record.
10. Dr. Kavita Kori (PW-6) stated that there were no internal or external injury marks on the body of the victim.
Her hymen was old torn.
There was no bleeding or any signs of injury on the body of the victim.
She could not give any opinion in regard to immediate violation of privacy of the victim.

11. When all these facts are taken into consideration, especially in view of the evidence of father of the victim (PW-2), who stated that, he is illiterate, he had recorded date of birth of the victim in the school on the basis of estimation and then as per the chronology of marriage and birth of children given by both the parents i.e. PW-2 & PW-4, the victim appears to be an adult.

Since school entries have not been proved, then in view of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Birad Mal Singhvi Vs. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16195 5 CRA-5263-2024 Anand Purohit, AIR 1988 SC 1796 , we are of the opinion that, the prosecution has failed to prove the date of birth of victim as recorded in the school record.

sentences.text: They did not produce the first school entry register.
The parents of the victim have admitted that the victim was an adult at the time of the incident.
The victim also admitted her adulthood and consent to the relationship.

12. When all these facts are taken into consideration, then a consensual relationship between two adults will not constitute offence either under the provisions of the POCSO Act or under Section 375 of IPC, so to attract the provisions of Section 376 IPC.

Thus, the impugned judgment dated 09.12.2023 passed by learned Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989) Betul, District Betul in case No.SCATR No.191/2020, overlooking these vital pieces of evidence, which are available on record, deserves to be and is hereby set-aside.
